item.title: EU touts ‘big interest’ in Algeria’s gas and green hydrogen
item.description: The EU wants to increase its stake in Algeria's gas and green hydrogen supplies, the bloc's energy commissioner said on Thursday.

item.title: Trump’s Greenland threat made Nato less ‘boring’, Rutte says
item.description: Nato chief Mark Rutte joked about Donald Trump's invasion threat, at the Western allies' first high-level meeting since the peak in the Greenland crisis.

item.title: Greece moves to arrest Nordic aid worker supporting migrants
item.description: Greek authorities have issued an European Arrest Warrant against Norwegian human rights activist Tommy Olsen, who leads the Aegean Boat Report, supporting migrants.

item.title: ‘Two-speed Europe’ and ‘Made in EU’ form core conclusions of leaders’ retreat
item.description: A "two‑speed Europe" plus a “European preference” took centre stage at the EU leaders’ informal retreat in Alden Biesen, Belgium — with a new roadmap of competitiveness reforms expected ahead of the March Brussels summit.

item.title: Europe’s machinery and pharma strengths give leverage over US and China, report finds
item.description: Europe hold over machines, pharmaceuticals in global supply chains can be used to deter and shape the behaviour of "systemic rivals" such as the United States and China, a new report finds.

item.title: From combat zone to the EU marketplace: the challenge for Ukraine’s farmers
item.description: Ukraine’s agriculture industry has faced numerous challenges since Russia’s 2022 invasion. While farmers have battled to maintain production, Ukraine's exports have caused friction with EU member states. What began as an emergency lifeline for a country at war has evolved into a structural shift — one now testing political solidarity inside the EU.

item.title: Spain’s 500,000 migrant regularisation — pragmatism or pull factor?
item.description: Spain’s move forces a harder conversation. Is it better to pretend half a million workers do not exist, or to regulate the reality already on the ground?

item.title: Anger as US report on EU ‘censorship’ leaves commission, NGOs’ names unredacted
item.description: The recent US report on 'EU censorship' left dozens of names of civil society and EU officials unredacted in emails – while carefully hiding company employee names.

item.title: More civilians killed in Ukraine last year than any other since Russia’s 2022 invasion
item.description: "There were more civilians killed and injured in 2025 than in the previous three years," Bernadette Castel-Hollingsworth, who heads the UN refugee agency's division in Ukraine, told EUobserver

item.title: Why is the EU struggling to scale artificial intelligence?
item.description: OpenAI spends more on AI than the whole EU. Europe is lagging in the innovation race — here’s why, and how it plans to catch up.
